content.text:
The message you just sent still has `<ELEMENT>` unfilled, so I assumed you mean the same thing as last time: the Code, Chain, Spec and Ask tabs in `ChatInputScope`. I read all 94 history entries and checked them against `spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi`, `src/chat_input.rs` and `src/prompt_mode.rs`. I didn't edit anything.

**What the spec already gets right, so the prompt skips it:** the Code, Spec and both system prompts. That a queued prompt keeps its mode. The Chain tab's broken and joined icons, its 50% dimming and its "Code and Spec" tooltip. That selecting Chain selects both Code and Spec. Escape, and that focus stays in the input while cycling tabs.

---

## Prompt for the spec agent

```
@{ChatInputScope} Here's how the tabs and the Ask tab should work.

**Tabs**
There are four tabs, in order: Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask. Code, Spec, and Ask are ordinary tabs using gpui-kit's default tab styling, sitting flush against each other with no extra gaps. Pressing <Tab> in the chat input cycles Code, Chain, Spec, Ask and back to Code; <Shift+Tab> goes the other way.

**Chain tab**
Chain is also a tab, just a small one because it only shows an icon. It never has a focus outline. While unselected it sits between Code and Spec, taking its own width like any other tab. When it's selected, it animates as though it gained a negative margin of half its width on both its left and right sides. Code and Spec slide together until they meet beneath it, and the chain sits centred on the seam, so Code and Spec read as one unified tab. Deselecting it animates them apart again. While selected, the chain has no left or right borders and a transparent background, so the selected Code and Spec show through beneath it, with no visible seam between them.

**Colour**
The selected tab and the tab body behind the input each get a subtle colour: red for Code, blue for Spec, and purple when Chain has both selected. Ask is green. The colour change is animated as a transition whenever the selection changes.

**Ask system prompt**
Ask is the mode for simply asking a question. Its systemPrompt, with the locations read from piton.config.pi like the other modes, is:

We're only asking a question about the code located in <code location> and the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit either of them.

**Asking**
A question sent from the Ask tab runs straight away, separately from any running Code, Spec, or Chain task. It never goes into the queue, so on the Ask tab the send button never reads "Queue". Its progress and results show in a task table that slides up out of the chat input, animated. While the harness is still thinking, the table is a single row just above the tabs. Once the question has finished, it expands into the full task table. While a question's panel is open, the message list behind it is dimmed to draw attention to the panel.
```

---

## Belongs in a different scope

- **Dimming the message list behind the Ask panel.** The prompt states it from the chat input's side. `MessageList` may also want to say it gets dimmed.
- **Keeping context between requests.** This belongs in `HarnessIntegrationScope`, which still describes one-off runs. Tasks and Ask each keep a conversation, and each send resumes it. Every send uses the mode's own system prompt even when resuming.
- **Ask questions staying out of the prompt history.** They're saved under `.suspense/asks` instead of `.suspense/history`. This belongs in `PromptEditor`, next to history and queue persistence.
- **A running question counts as work when quitting.** This belongs in `MainWindowScope`, with the quit confirmation, which isn't in the spec yet either.
- **Skeletons, raw JSON preview and tool placeholders** in the Ask row. These belong in `MessageList`.

## Choices the agent made that you never asked for

- **Ask colours:** Ask is green, and I put that in the prompt. Remove it if you don't want it.
- **Ask's system prompt:** you asked for "don't edit src/ or spec/", but the exact sentence was the agent's.
- **Tint strength:** 10% opacity, sliding through the colours in between. Going from Code to Ask passes through purple and blue.
- **Ask tab width:** it stretches to the right edge of the tab bar.
- **Chain animation:** it uses a spring with no bounce. While joined, the chain covers about 20px of Code and of Spec, so clicks there select Chain.
- **Tab key with the completion menu open:** Tab goes to the menu instead of switching tabs.
- **One question at a time:** asking a new question replaces a running one and stops it.
- **Close button:** an X closes the Ask panel, and stops the question if it's still running.
- **Panel sizes:** the single row is 80px tall. The finished panel is up to 400px, and its output scrolls past 320px. It covers the bottom of the message list.
- **Dimming:** the list dims to 45% black, fading more slowly than the slide. Clicks still go through to the list, and an open file beside the list isn't dimmed.
- **Ask output isn't kept:** it's gone once you close the panel or restart.
- **Context between requests** (my changes from earlier this session):
  - Ask and tasks each have their own conversation, not one shared one.
  - Tasks pick up the latest conversation from history after a restart; Ask's conversation is lost on restart.
  - A conversation that fails to resume is dropped.
  - There's no way to start a fresh conversation.

## Contradictions that couldn't be settled

- **Fresh context or kept context.** You first said "Every new prompt/task send should be a fresh context", then later asked for sending to "maintain context between requests". The later request wins, but it doesn't say whether Ask and tasks should share one conversation or keep separate ones. It also doesn't say whether context should survive a restart.
- **Chain selection.** The spec says Code, Chain and Spec "all show as selected". Your latest requests say the selected chain has a transparent background and no side borders. I went with the latest, so only Code and Spec look selected underneath the chain.

**One warning about sending this:** your last three runs of this request failed to compile because the text contained `@{ScopeName}`. In prompts sent through the app, the only `@{...}` should be real references like `@{ChatInputScope}`.
